title: BTS boycott Grammys after introduction of new Asian pop category
facts: South Korean music group BTS announced they will not submit their music for the upcoming Grammy Awards.
The Recording Academy introduced five new award categories, including Best Asian Pop Music Performance.
BTS released their comeback studio album titled 'ARIRANG' following mandatory military service.
BTS became the first all-South Korean music act to reach number one on the Billboard Hot 100 with 'Dynamite' in 2020.
Harvey Mason Jr. serves as Chief Executive Officer of the Recording Academy.
The Best Asian Pop Music Performance Grammy category requires musical entries to contain meaningful use of an Asian language.
BTS's album 'ARIRANG' features predominantly English lyrics.
Lee Ji-young is a professor at Hankuk University of Foreign Studies.
BTS donated $1 million to the Black Lives Matter movement in 2020.
BTS addressed the White House in 2022 on the topics of anti-Asian hate and social inclusivity.
BTS performed a halftime musical showcase at the 2026 FIFA World Cup final in the United States.
BTS consists of seven band members who posted coordinated boycott announcements on Instagram.
BTS previously earned Grammy nominations including Best Music Video without winning an award.
The Recording Academy created the Asian Pop category to recognize music genres including K-pop, J-pop, and C-pop.
BTS concluded a concert tour across Europe prior to their Grammy boycott announcement.
